techniques.label: Word cycler
techniques.desc: AnimatePresence mode='wait' — rotates value props through a single line on interval

techniques.label: Editorial pull quote
techniques.desc: Manual line breaks via display:block spans, 4-step color scale for reading rhythm

techniques.label: GIF illustrations
techniques.desc: Screen recordings → Gifski-compressed GIFs used as feature section visuals

techniques.label: Jumbo wordmark
techniques.desc: 8906px-wide PNG as hero centrepiece — type treated as image

techniques.label: H-scroll masonry
techniques.desc: Mixed portrait/landscape card heights create visual rhythm in draggable row

techniques.label: Bento UI cards
techniques.desc: Fake-but-realistic UI mockups as section illustrations — no icons, no stock photos

techniques.label: Infinite marquee
techniques.desc: Doubled list + single CSS translateX(-50%) keyframe. No library needed.

techniques.label: Drag carousel
techniques.desc: Framer Scroll component set to horizontal — zero JS, native gesture

techniques.label: Depth via fill value
techniques.desc: Slightly lighter bg fills create elevation over dark bg — no box-shadow needed

techniques.label: Micro-illustrations
techniques.desc: Step-process widgets with contextual animated UI previews per step

techniques.label: Corner bracket markers
techniques.desc: L-shaped divs at card corners — 4 absolute-positioned elements, each showing only 2 borders for HUD aesthetic

techniques.label: Glassmorphism cards
techniques.desc: backdrop-filter: blur(20px) + rgba(255,255,255,0.05) bg + 1px border at ~12% opacity

techniques.label: Organic wave chart
techniques.desc: SVG cubic bezier path fills, two overlapping translucent areas for market vs portfolio comparison

techniques.label: Avatar arc network
techniques.desc: Circular avatars positioned along a curved SVG path — simulates a social graph with CSS transforms

techniques.label: Radial dot matrix
techniques.desc: background: radial-gradient(circle, rgba(255,255,255,0.15) 1px, transparent 1px) @ 16px/16px repeat

techniques.label: Icon-first card structure
techniques.desc: Centered icon circle → heading → description → UI illustration. Top-down reading: symbol, concept, proof

techniques.label: SVG connection tree
techniques.desc: Brand logos joined by SVG line paths converging to a single central node — API integration metaphor

techniques.label: Scrolling word cloud
techniques.desc: Vertical/diagonal grid of capability words scrolling behind a centred auth badge

techniques.label: Waveform illustration
techniques.desc: SVG rect bars of varying heights — classic speech/audio visualization pattern

techniques.label: Noise grain texture
techniques.desc: SVG feTurbulence filter or semi-transparent PNG overlay applied to card surfaces

techniques.label: Perspective-tilted product UI
techniques.desc: CSS perspective + rotateX/rotateY on the dashboard screenshot creates the classic 3D product hero tilt

techniques.label: Floating annotation badges
techniques.desc: Pill labels positioned outside the tilted card frame — breaks the box, implies depth

techniques.label: Stacked card scatter
techniques.desc: Multiple overlapping cards at different rotation angles suggest a physical desk of assets

techniques.label: 3D CGI asset renders
techniques.desc: Isometric 3D renders of real-world assets used as category illustrations — not photos

techniques.label: Soft lavender gradient bg
techniques.desc: Light mode linear-gradient from near-white to soft #e8e8ff — never pure white

title: Stripe
subtitle: Financial Infrastructure to Grow Your Revenue
creator: Stripe Design Team

techniques.label: Animated gradient wave hero
techniques.desc: WebGL canvas animation with shifting indigo/purple/teal/coral mesh — static PNG fallback for reduced-motion

techniques.label: Mixed-weight typographic emphasis
techniques.desc: Italic serif mixed with sans in the same headline — typeface contrast as emphasis, not size

techniques.label: Gradient text via background-clip
techniques.desc: background-clip: text; color: transparent — letters carry the brand gradient range

techniques.label: Bento product grid
techniques.desc: Asymmetric large + small cards, each with high-fidelity mini product UI as illustration

techniques.label: Border-only elevation
techniques.desc: Cards use 1px border at 8% opacity — zero box-shadow, elevation via bg tint contrast

techniques.label: Radial particle burst
techniques.desc: HTML5 Canvas 2D, no WebGL. Particles fan from a bottom-centre origin with random angle/maxLen/speed. Opacity eases in (0–15% of travel), holds (15–70%), fades out (70–100%). clearRect + requestAnimationFrame loop — dot tip drawn with ctx.arc at the line endpoint.

techniques.label: Staggered card reveal
techniques.desc: Each card starts at opacity:0 + translateY(22px). setTimeout fires per card at index × staggerMs delay. cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) spring ease-out snaps cards into place.

techniques.label: IntersectionObserver trigger
techniques.desc: Stagger fires once when 20% of the section enters viewport — no scroll listeners, no layout thrash. observe(section) → animateCards() on entry.

techniques.label: Clip-path word reveal
techniques.desc: Headline words wrapped in overflow:hidden divs. Each word slides up from translateY(110%) with animation-delay: calc(var(--i) * 0.08s) — the wrapping div clips the motion.

techniques.label: Multi-layer radial gradient bg
techniques.desc: 3 overlapping radial-gradient blobs at different positions/colours layered on a dark base. Each blob at ~30% opacity — stacking creates the painted, glowing look.

techniques.label: Product as marketing medium
techniques.desc: The page IS built like a Gamma presentation — card-based sections, cinematic transitions, content-first layout. The design demonstrates the product by embodying it.

title: Instrument
subtitle: Design Studio — Campaign US Agency of the Year 2026
creator: Instrument Studio

techniques.label: Masonry case study grid
techniques.desc: Mixed portrait and landscape thumbnails in an auto-filling CSS grid — no fixed rows, each image fills its natural aspect ratio. Creates editorial variety without manual placement.

techniques.label: Hover-reveal metadata
techniques.desc: Client name and category tags are hidden by default, revealed on hover via opacity + translateY transition. Keeps the grid visually clean — images speak first.

techniques.label: Category tag system
techniques.desc: #BRAND #MARKETING #PRODUCT as filterable taxonomy. Tags use monospace uppercase at small size — typographic restraint signals design confidence.

techniques.label: Full-bleed image cards
techniques.desc: No card borders, no padding, no rounded corners on the grid items — images bleed edge-to-edge inside their cells. White gutters do all the separation work.

techniques.label: Typeface as identity
techniques.desc: Instrument uses a custom/distinctive display typeface for the studio name — the wordmark IS the brand. No icon, no logomark.

techniques.label: Display serif at hero scale
techniques.desc: Large transitional serif sets the headline at magazine-cover scale — financial product speaking in editorial cadence. Sans handles body copy.

techniques.label: Wireframe isometric illustration
techniques.desc: Two stacked cubes drawn as a single-weight lime line — no fill, no shading. Stand-in for the deposit vault, concept-first.

techniques.label: Bordered-vs-filled CTA pair
techniques.desc: Identical pill geometry; only the fill swaps. Outlined Log In + filled Sign Up — primary/secondary hierarchy in one shape language.

techniques.label: Single-accent reduction
techniques.desc: Whole page lives on black + white text + one lime. Buttons, illustration, and wordmark all share the same hue — colour as constraint.

techniques.label: Editorial promo split
techniques.desc: Headline left, illustration right — no cards, no backgrounds, no scaffolding. Whitespace and typographic scale carry the composition.

techniques.label: Two-tone split layout
techniques.desc: Page bisected vertically — cool azure left for the swap product, soft pink right for the wallet. Two products, one surface, each panel keeping its own colour identity.

techniques.label: Headlines in section accent
techniques.desc: Explore. Swap. Repeat. in cyan. Simple. Safe. Secure. in magenta. Type itself carries the brand hue, not just buttons — every word on a panel matches the panel.

techniques.label: Three-beat triplet headlines
techniques.desc: Both sides use period-separated triplets in the same syntax. A brand cadence built into the headline pattern — repeated structure as recall device.

techniques.label: Token rows as illustration
techniques.desc: Live-styled price rows (Ethereum $2,300.15 +0.59%) with real logos and colour-coded change. The product UI doubles as the marketing graphic — no separate hero illustration needed.

techniques.label: Tinted action-tile grid
techniques.desc: Wallet preview shows four pill action tiles (card, send, receive, scan), each with a tinted bg matching its icon hue. Adds texture without breaking the soft-pastel palette.

title: Harvey
subtitle: AI Platform for Legal Work
creator: Harvey AI
style: Dark Editorial Legal SaaS — Product Accordion

techniques.label: Active-section accordion
techniques.desc: Vertical capability list (Client engagement, Due diligence, Drafting, Research, Negotiation) where the open one expands to show body copy + paired product screen on the right; siblings collapse to a title row. One-at-a-time disclosure used as section navigation.

techniques.label: Real product UI as illustration
techniques.desc: Vault / Change of Control Analysis screen docks right of the active section — Filter / Add file / Column builder chips, file table with Yes/No provision pills. Marketing visual = product surface itself, no commissioned mock.

techniques.label: Whisper-grey title hierarchy
techniques.desc: Inactive section titles fade to mid-grey on near-black; only the active one promotes to white. Identical weight and size across all five — hierarchy carried purely through value contrast.

techniques.label: Tonal inset, no border
techniques.desc: Right-side product card sits on a barely-lighter grey rectangle whose edge is a soft tonal step, not a stroke. Window-without-card — depth without chrome.

techniques.label: Persistent Ask Harvey pill
techniques.desc: Bottom-right floating pill (serif H mark + 'Ask Harvey' label) stays anchored across sections. Brand AI surface as page chrome rather than a help-widget afterthought.

techniques.label: Oil painting hosts the IDE
techniques.desc: A 19th-century romantic landscape — slate peak, sage lake, cliffs in haze — fills the lower hero. The Cursor Desktop window sits centred on the painting like a figure on a canvas. Argument by juxtaposition: the warmth of human-made art hosting the cold structure of code. Art and technology in one frame.

techniques.label: Stacked product windows
techniques.desc: A second smaller Cursor CLI window overlaps the desktop one bottom-right — same painting backdrop bleeding behind both. Reads like a torn-out detail of the larger view, signalling the product spans surfaces (GUI + terminal) without two separate sections.

techniques.label: Cream-paper page bg
techniques.desc: Whole page lives on warm oat-cream rather than white. Pairs with the painting's tonal range — the page feels printed, not screen-glaring. No gradients, no glow, no SaaS sheen.

techniques.label: Display sans at hero scale
techniques.desc: Wide grotesque sans set 2-line, full bleed, near-black on cream. No eyebrow, no preheader — the headline carries the entire upper hero alone. Confidence through restraint.

techniques.label: Mass-contrast pill CTA pair
techniques.desc: Solid black 'Get started →' + transparent ghost 'Request a demo →'. Same pill geometry, opposite fill — mass primary, ghost secondary. Trailing arrows do the affordance work, no chevrons or icons.

title: Framer
subtitle: No-Code Site Builder
creator: Framer
style: Black Product Accordion — Editor Over Output

techniques.label: Editor over rendered output
techniques.desc: Framer's 'Fill' settings panel floats in front of a browser chrome that itself contains a rendered customer site. Three layers stacked into one composition: tool → canvas → output. Shows the product operating on the work, not just resulting in it.

techniques.label: Real customer site as demo canvas
techniques.desc: The browser frame loads an actual Framer-built portfolio (baseform.framer.website — 'We craft digital brands with bold sp...'), complete with editorial fashion photography below. Marketing demo = live customer work, not a stylised mock.

techniques.label: Active-section accordion list
techniques.desc: Vertical capability nav (AI, Design, CMS, Collaborate) where the active item expands to body copy + 'Learn more →'; siblings collapse to title-only and fade to mid-grey. Hierarchy by chroma, not by indicator bar or chevron.

techniques.label: Browser chrome as picture frame
techniques.desc: Mac traffic lights + URL bar + thin cyan selection ring wrap the demo. Product output presented as a real window — implies the site is running live, not a flat screenshot.

techniques.label: Editor panel breaks the frame
techniques.desc: The Fill panel anchors bottom-third and intentionally breaks the browser's right edge. Off-grid placement signals the editor is *acting on* the canvas, not part of the canvas's chrome.

title: Laws of UX
subtitle: UX Heuristics, Illustrated
creator: Jon Yablonski
style: Editorial Reference — Bauhaus Illustration on Parchment

techniques.label: Illustrations that demonstrate the law
techniques.desc: Choice Overload card shows a grid of cream dots scattered across a blue field — overwhelming choice made visible. Chunking shows the same dots regrouped into an 'F' shape — literal grouping demo. Aesthetic-Usability uses a clean triangle-on-circle Bauhaus mark — the principle itself aesthetically pleasing. Each illustration IS a working example of the law named beside it.

techniques.label: Bauhaus-modernist illustration system
techniques.desc: Flat geometry, two-tone within each card, circle/square/triangle primitives, no shading or gradients. Period-correct visual vocabulary borrowed from mid-century pedagogy — pairs the old discipline of design teaching with timeless heuristics.

techniques.label: Warm parchment paper bg
techniques.desc: Whole page lives on dusty cream rather than white. Faint outlined circles drift behind the headline as decorative geometry. Reads like a printed reference book in the Designing With the Mind In Mind / Tufte lineage — not a webpage.

techniques.label: Display serif as opening line
techniques.desc: Lead copy set in a transitional serif at editorial scale, flush-left, no eyebrow or chrome above it. The page presents itself as a book opening, not a marketing pitch.

techniques.label: Small-caps top nav
techniques.desc: ARTICLES · BOOK · CARDS · INFO · STORE in spaced uppercase. Wide letterspacing — institutional, museum-label cadence. Anchors the editorial tone before any content loads.

title: Ramp
subtitle: All-in-One Spend Management
creator: Ramp
style: Editorial Cream Fintech — Black + Lime, Live Odometers

techniques.label: Live odometer stat counters
techniques.desc: Hero stat (US Corporate Payments Processed By Ramp: 0.6934860%) and the footer ribbon both tick in real time — rolling-digit odometers turn ambient data into motion. Operational metrics replace stock hero animation.

techniques.label: Pill email capture
techniques.desc: Single rounded pill holds a transparent email input + lime 'Get started for free' button as one continuous unit. The CTA sits inside the input frame — submission affordance and form share one shape.

techniques.label: Macro-editorial headline
techniques.desc: 'Time is money. Save Both.' set at magazine-cover scale, heavy grotesque, near-black on warm cream — no eyebrow, no preheader. Headline alone carries the upper hero, fintech speaking in editorial cadence.

techniques.label: Dotted-paper page bg
techniques.desc: Faint dot grid covers the whole canvas at very low opacity — receipt / ledger paper texture without breaking the minimal palette. Adds tactility to a white-heavy layout.

techniques.label: Stacked product surface mockups
techniques.desc: macOS-chrome window showing the Bills page docks centred; a smaller phone mockup overlaps bottom-right with the matching mobile view. One product across two surfaces in a single composition — desktop + mobile without two separate sections.

techniques.label: Agents-at-work footer ribbon
techniques.desc: Full-width bottom bar of six ticking counters — accounting fields coded, agent interactions, expenses reviewed, spend allocated, invoices processed, violations classified. Operational dashboard as social proof — work happening live, not testimonials in past tense.

title: Legend
subtitle: Onchain Money Superapp
creator: Legend Labs
style: Editorial DeFi in Nature — CGI Landscape + Glass Portfolio

techniques.label: CGI landscape hosts the product
techniques.desc: Photoreal grass-and-rocks meadow with low rolling fog fills the lower hero; a translucent phone-style portfolio card floats centred over it. DeFi pulled out of dashboard-on-gradient marketing into something elemental — the product appears to live in nature, not over an abstract hero.

techniques.label: Cycling verb + colour swap
techniques.desc: 'Own your future. ● Earn up to 11.59%' — verb and icon rotate (Earn / Borrow / …) and the entire colour identity swaps with them (green for Earn, purple for Borrow). Not just text swap — hue, icon, and rate all change as one unit.

techniques.label: Compass coordinates as page chrome
techniques.desc: 47.0514° N / 9.0678° E set in monospace small-caps floating in the upper canvas margins. Real-world coordinates as decorative frame — gives the landscape a sense of place and signals geographic identity in a category that usually pretends to be placeless.

techniques.label: Translucent glass portfolio card
techniques.desc: Phone-sized portfolio sits frosted over the meadow with rocks and grass legible through the surface. No opaque card, no drop-shadow scaffolding — the product UI feels weightless against the world behind it. Glass over photography, not card over gradient.

techniques.label: Dashed architectural gridlines
techniques.desc: Faint vertical and horizontal dashed lines run across the canvas like working drawings. Frames the composition with structure without panels — design presented as draft, not finished marketing art.

techniques.label: Wind-down notice as page chrome
techniques.desc: Pill-shaped top banner with a soft orange status dot — 'Legend is winding down in 58 days. Please withdraw your funds. Read Announcement →'. Even the deprecation message is shaped as polished page chrome, not a system alert ribbon.

title: Maze
subtitle: User Research and Testing Platform
creator: Maze
style: Lime Tonal Manifesto — Marquee Feature Pills

techniques.label: Paragraph as hero copy
techniques.desc: Instead of a punchy short headline, the hero is a full 3-line sentence set at display scale — 'Companies recruit the right participants effortlessly, conduct research autonomously, and deliver user insights that drive actual decisions.' Reads as a manifesto, not a tagline.

techniques.label: Tonal monochrome page
techniques.desc: Saturated lime fills the whole canvas; copy is set in a darker olive of the same hue. Same colour, two values — no contrast switch, no accent pop. Confidence to live inside a single chord.

techniques.label: Marquee feature pills
techniques.desc: Horizontal infinite-scroll rows of capability pills (Easily embeddable results · Card sorting · Tree testing · Surveys · Participant management · Screener questions · B2B or B2C participants). Feature taxonomy presented as moving typography rather than a static grid.

techniques.label: Edge-clipped pills
techniques.desc: Pills at the canvas edges are cut mid-letter ('nts...' / 'S...'). Implies the row keeps going, never fully visible — always-revealing layout that makes breadth feel inexhaustible without listing it out.

techniques.label: Two-row offset marquee
techniques.desc: Top and bottom pill rows are staggered horizontally so different pills surface at each x-position. Creates a parallax-of-content sense — the platform is wider than the screen, sliced two ways.

techniques.label: Mass-contrast CTA trio
techniques.desc: Tiny top-right cluster: ghost 'Log in' text, outlined pill 'Try Maze', solid black 'Contact sales'. Three actions, three levels of mass — hierarchy carried by fill weight on near-identical geometry.

title: Statsig
subtitle: Measure What Ships. Ship What Matters.
creator: Statsig
style: Enterprise Experimentation SaaS — Cream + Indigo, Stacked Dashboards

techniques.label: Stacked product surfaces
techniques.desc: Two product UI windows — an experiment-results card (CUPED · Sequential Testing) behind a metrics-and-chart panel — overlap on a diagonal. Two product views in one composition, depth via offset rather than z-stack chrome.

techniques.label: Methodology chips as authenticity tell
techniques.desc: Filter chips read CUPED · Sequential Testing — real statistical methods with green-check status, not Filter 1 / Filter 2 placeholder text. Marketing demo uses authentic stats vocabulary; the technical audience reads it as credibility, everyone else as professionalism.

techniques.label: Three-layer area chart
techniques.desc: Daily comparison chart shows three overlapping translucent area fills (grey baseline, green variant, blue variant) along a jagged shared timeline. Live experimentation output IS the hero illustration — no abstract decoration.

techniques.label: Soft cream off-white page bg
techniques.desc: Whole page lives on warm near-white rather than pure white. Pairs with muted indigo/green chart fills — feels printed reference paper, not SaaS-glaring. Same restraint Ramp and Cursor lean on.

techniques.label: Mass-contrast CTA pair
techniques.desc: Solid black 'Create a free account' pill + ghost 'See how it works' pill at hero centre. Same geometry, opposite fill — primary by mass, secondary by outline. Mirrored in the upper-right Sign In / Contact Us nav pair.

techniques.label: Logo wall as hero base
techniques.desc: Eight customer wordmarks (OpenAI, Brex, Televisa Univision, Microsoft, Atlassian, Decathlon, Milwaukee, Riot Games) sit in monotone grey directly below the product mockup — no 'Trusted by' header. Names alone do the social-proof work.

title: Reducto
subtitle: Agentic Document Platform
creator: Reducto
style: Continuous-Form Print — Tractor-Feed Margins, Wireframe Illustrations

techniques.label: Tractor-feed paper margins
techniques.desc: Round perforation holes run top-to-bottom down both left and right margins — the look of continuous-form printer paper. Pure structural texture frames the canvas as machine output / API document, the brand metaphor embedded in the page chrome itself.

techniques.label: Hairline grid-cell layout
techniques.desc: Features sit inside an explicit 3-column light-grey grid where each cell is bordered with a single 1px line. No cards, no shadows, no fills — information density via hairlines. Reads like a spec sheet, not a brochure.

techniques.label: Bounding-box pointer illustrations
techniques.desc: Layout extraction shows a blank wireframe doc with tiny grey labels (table, text, figure) pointing to specific regions via leader lines. The illustration IS the product output — what Reducto returns when it parses a page, rendered as the marketing visual.

techniques.label: Greeting-pill polyglot proof
techniques.desc: Language support shows Olá · Hello · வணக்கம் · こんにちは · Merhaba · 你好 · 안녕하세요 · Привіт as scattered pills, some with green-check status. Multilingual coverage demonstrated through actual character glyphs — no flags, no counters, no list of language names.

techniques.label: Single-hue spotlight cycler
techniques.desc: Below the cubes illustration, three captions (Figure summarization / Graph extraction / Automatic page rotation) are listed in grey except Graph extraction, which is set in brand purple. A cycling spotlight that highlights one capability at a time within a fixed list — animation hinted, not labelled.

techniques.label: Dot-matrix grayscale page mockups
techniques.desc: File type support shows three stacked document thumbnails (.jpeg / .xlsx tabs) rendered as dotted grayscale fills rather than literal screenshots. Period-correct printer-paper aesthetic — every illustration looks scanned, not designed.

title: Binance.US
subtitle: Crypto Trading in the U.S.
creator: Binance.US
style: Fintech Markets Index — Yellow CTA, Heat-Map Change Pills

techniques.label: Heat-map change pills
techniques.desc: Daily Change column renders every value inside a filled rounded rectangle — red for losses, green for gains. The single column becomes a wall of color blocks; the screen reads as a sentiment heat map at a glance, even at small text size.

techniques.label: Brand-owned token glyphs
techniques.desc: Each row leads with the token's own circular brand mark (Bitcoin orange, Ethereum blue, USDT teal, BNB yellow, XRP black, USDC blue, Solana gradient). Identity carried by real logos rather than stand-in monograms — the table inherits the entire crypto-asset visual vocabulary.

techniques.label: Per-row sparkline column
techniques.desc: A faint two-color line chart sits inside the Chart column for every row, identical width, micro-canvas. Adds quick visual context per token without leaving the index view — chart as a column-type, not a separate page.

techniques.label: Yellow pill as single action language
techniques.desc: Every row's 'Trade' button is the same filled yellow pill with a chart icon, repeated 50+ times down the page. Pairs with upper-right yellow 'Sign Up'. One colour does all primary-action duty — brand hue as CTA signal, not decoration.

techniques.label: Active-by-border filter pills
techniques.desc: All (53) / Top Gainers / Top Losers / Trending — pill row where the active state is signalled by yellow border colour, not by fill swap. Preserves a single horizontal rhythm; selection reads as outline shift, no mass change.

techniques.label: Star-favourite leading column
techniques.desc: Every row begins with a faint outlined star — one-click watchlist add inline with the table. No 'Favorites' tab, no separate UI surface — the action lives at the row level where the eye already is.

techniques.label: Editorial promo chip strip
techniques.desc: Top announcement uses a near-black pill ('Trade with the lowest fees in the U.S.') sitting on a pale green strip, with green dollar mark. Promotional language as a standalone editorial chip — not a banner with noisy bg-color.

title: Google Research
subtitle: Research, to reality.
creator: Google Research
style: Editorial White — Cutout Collage + Hand-Drawn Marks

techniques.label: Headline broken across the hero
techniques.desc: 'Research,' sits top-left and 'to reality.' drops bottom-right at the same display scale — the title is split diagonally across whitespace so the collage objects (butterfly, satellite) live inside the line break rather than beside it. The gap between the two halves IS the composition.

techniques.label: Photo-cutout collage objects
techniques.desc: A real monarch butterfly and a masked satellite render float as cut-out photography against pure white — no card, no frame, no shadow. Mixes literal science imagery into the typographic field like a scrapbook spread, not a hero illustration block.

techniques.label: Hand-drawn arc accents
techniques.desc: Sketchy pencil-textured arcs and a circle are scattered around the hero — one curls top-right with an arrowhead, another rings the 'Amplifying human ingenuity' heading. Imperfect human marks deliberately offset the precision of a tech-giant brand.

techniques.label: Brand-dot punctuation
techniques.desc: A single Google-blue dot and a yellow dot are dropped into the whitespace as floating accents — the four-colour brand palette reduced to two stray points instead of a logo. Identity carried by placement, not a wordmark.

techniques.label: Black film card anchor
techniques.desc: A full-width black 'Google Research' video panel with a centred YouTube glyph and 'Watch the film' pill grounds the airy white hero — one heavy dark mass balancing all the floating light elements above it.
